hook_text: Why are the tallest buildings in a city always bunched together in one place?
clip_script: Every city is divided into zones. In the middle is the CBD, the central business district. It is where the main roads and railways meet, so everyone can reach it, so everyone wants to be there, so the land costs a fortune. That is why developers build up: ten floors on one plot means ten times the space. Banks, offices, big shops, taxi ranks and the train station. Further out: light industry, clothing and food factories near the main roads. Further still: heavy industry, steelworks and refineries, with railways, harbours and a lot of space, and hopefully a long way from homes. Accessibility. Land value. Needs. That is how to read a city.
visual_style: A whiteboard city drawn from the side and from above: a cluster of towers in the centre, low warehouses around them, and chimneys and tanks at the edge beside a railway.
pacing: Quick reveals zone by zone, with a pause on the floor space idea.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn how to spot zones on maps and photos.
